author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: I am prepared to accept the risk assessment remaining a manual process for this release. The physical stock is already committed to the supplier, so we cannot wait for a fully automated validation pipeline to be built from scratch. However, this flexibility comes with a strict condition. The acceptance criteria for the allocation logic must be fully governed. I need a formal, strict sign off on those criteria before the trucks leave the distribution centre. If the criteria are not governed, I will not approve the deployment, regardless of the manual risk checks. This ensures the logic is auditable and protects us from compliance issues if the promotion underperforms.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are prepared to accept the risk of a manual process in exchange for the speed of the release, which fits the definition of giving up a preference (automation) to gain another (timeliness).
